newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's parliament to discuss MMT bill today.
newsitem.headline: Canada's parliament to discuss MMT bill today.

text.p: A controversial bill to ban the gasoline additive MMT will is scheduled for debate in Canada's House of Commons on Wednesday afternoon, parliament said on Wednesday.
The bill, which aims to ban the import and interprovincial trade of MMT, faces a final debate before a vote by the House of Commons, the Canadian parliament's lower chamber.

The debate will be preceded by a speech by Environment Minister Sergio Marchi, who reintroduced the bill last spring after it was set aside at the end of parliament's session in February. If it passes the House of Commons vote, the bill will go to the Senate for final approval before becoming law.
MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, is a fuel octane enhancer. It has been used as a replacement for lead in gasoline in Canada since 1977.

Two weeks ago, Richmond, Va.-based Ethyl Corp, threatened Ottawa with a US$201 million lawsuit under the North American Free Trade Agreement in a bid to stop the bill. Ethyl Corp is the parent of Ethyl Canada, the sole manufacturer of MMT in the country.
But Marchi said he would continue to press the bill in parliament despite the lawsuit.
The use of MMT in the United States has been permitted since late 1995 after a U.S. Court of Appeals overruled Environmental Protection Agency objections to the additive.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
